title: Loyola University Chicago students protest as Title IX mishandling lawsuit heads toward 2027 trial
summary: Students rallied on campus over a lawsuit by ten former students alleging the university mishandled and underreported sexual assault complaints dating back to 2011. The university has failed to get the case dismissed, and a trial is set for September 2027; Loyola declined to comment on pending litigation.

title: Former student sues Evergreen Public Schools, alleging district failed to stop band teacher's abuse
institution: Evergreen Public Schools (Mountain View High School)
summary: A former Mountain View High School student filed suit in Clark County Superior Court alleging the district failed to protect her from years of grooming and sexual abuse by a band teacher in the early 2000s. The claims are allegations and have not been tested in court.

title: Englewood school district sued over alleged abuse by after-school program aide
summary: A new lawsuit against the Englewood school board, the city and an elementary school alleges officials knew or should have known about the conduct of a former after-school program aide who was arrested in 2023 on multiple sexual assault charges. The suit claims negligence and failure to supervise; the district had not commented.

title: Lyft asks federal judge to narrow consolidated passenger sexual assault lawsuits
summary: At a hearing in San Francisco, Lyft argued that negligence and product liability claims in roughly 136 consolidated federal suits by riders alleging assault by drivers should be dismissed. The judge voiced skepticism of some of Lyft's arguments but did not rule from the bench.

title: Cornell president acknowledges he never followed up on 2024 fraternity gang-rape report
summary: Cornell's president said he did not check the outcome of a student's 2024 report of a fraternity gang rape, as a lawsuit alleges the university mishandled her complaints and the faculty senate weighs a no-confidence resolution. New York's governor named the state attorney general special prosecutor and ordered an independent review of Cornell's handling of the case.

title: Federal judge rejects Oakland Diocese bankruptcy plan covering about 330 abuse claims
summary: A federal bankruptcy judge declined to confirm the Oakland Diocese's Chapter 11 plan meant to resolve roughly 330 clergy abuse claims, citing insufficient evidentiary support. The judge indicated a revised plan could still be approved.

title: Former Menlo-Atherton student sues Sequoia Union High School District over alleged teacher abuse
institution: Sequoia Union High School District (Menlo-Atherton High School)
summary: A former student filed suit in San Mateo County alleging a former teacher sexually abused her between 2006 and 2010 and that the district failed to supervise, investigate, warn students or report the teacher to police. The district did not respond to requests for comment.

title: Uber settles third bellwether passenger assault case in Texas just before opening statements
summary: Uber reached a confidential settlement with a Texas rider shortly after jury selection in the third bellwether trial of the federal passenger sexual assault litigation. Thousands of similar cases remain pending in the multidistrict litigation in California.

title: Education Department opens probes into NYC schools and Jeffco over staff sexual misconduct handling
institution: New York City Department of Education
summary: The U.S. Education Department's Office for Civil Rights launched investigations into how the New York City school system, Colorado's Jeffco Public Schools and unnamed districts in six other states handle sexual misconduct claims against employees, targeting so-called pass-the-trash practices. New York City schools said they take abuse allegations seriously and are reviewing the complaint.
location: United States, New York and Colorado

title: Second former student joins Child Victims Act suit against Montgomery County school board
summary: An amended complaint adds a second former elementary student to a lawsuit alleging the school board negligently kept a teacher in roles with access to children despite complaints dating to 1993 and a 1995 child protective services finding. The suit relies on Maryland's Child Victims Act; the allegations are unproven.

title: Massachusetts AG report finds hundreds of clergy abused nearly 1,000 children in three dioceses
institution: Dioceses of Worcester, Springfield and Fall River
summary: The Massachusetts attorney general released the state's first investigation into clergy abuse in three Catholic dioceses, finding that more than 270 clergy abused close to 1,000 children going back to the 1950s. The report notes Worcester remains the only diocese in the state without a public list of credibly accused priests.

title: Jury awards $164 million against College Park hotel operator in child sex trafficking case
summary: A federal jury in Atlanta found the operator of a College Park Super 8 liable under federal trafficking law, concluding it knew or should have known of trafficking at the property and profited from it. The verdict totaled $164 million.

title: Family sues Savannah nursing home alleging cover-up of resident sexual assault
summary: A lawsuit in Chatham County alleges a Savannah nursing facility failed to protect a nonverbal resident from sexual assault by another resident with a known history of misconduct and delayed informing her family. The facility had not responded to the allegations.

title: Former federal prison worker sentenced for sexual contact with inmates at FCI Thomson
summary: Danny L. Spyker, a former corrections officer and cook supervisor convicted by a federal jury of sexual contact with inmates, was sentenced to three years and five months in prison. Prosecutors said he abused his position of authority over people in custody.

title: Lawsuit alleges former Burnet County jail officer sexually abused a detainee
summary: A former detainee filed a federal lawsuit against Burnet County and former detention officer Michael Jason Wilson alleging he sexually abused her in custody in 2024. The article notes Wilson was previously convicted on felony counts involving abuse of a different detainee; the new claims are allegations.

title: Lawsuit alleges Genesis Health Clubs trainer groomed and abused a teenage member
summary: A former member alleges in a Jackson County, Missouri, lawsuit that a personal trainer at a Kansas City Genesis gym sexually abused her when she was a minor in 2021. The suit accuses the chain of negligent hiring, supervision and training.

title: Former Cal softball player sues UC Regents, alleging coach pursued coercive sexual relationship
summary: A former pitcher sued the University of California Regents and a former head softball coach, alleging a coercive sexual relationship and that the university was negligent in hiring, training and supervising staff who allegedly knew and did not intervene. The coach's tenure ended in 2025 shortly after the university received a report about the relationship.

title: Florida court enters judgment against prison health contractor over gynecologist abuse claims
summary: A federal court entered a $100,000 judgment in a civil case brought by five women prisoners alleging sexual abuse by a contracted gynecologist at Lowell Correctional Institution. The suit also alleged the state prison health contractor tolerated the conduct despite complaints; the doctor denies the allegations.

title: Appeals court orders new trial after $10 million verdict against Carnival in shipboard assault suit
summary: The 11th Circuit vacated parts of a $10.3 million Miami jury award to a passenger who alleged a crew member sexually assaulted her aboard a Carnival ship in 2018. The court ruled the jury should have been allowed to hear evidence from an FBI report and ordered a new trial.

title: Ireland's schools abuse commission invites survivors to share experiences in national survey
institution: Religious-run and other Irish schools (Commission of Investigation)
summary: The state Commission of Investigation into historical sexual abuse in Irish schools is launching a survey of people abused in schools between 1927 and 2013 to identify patterns and guide its inquiry. A 2024 scoping inquiry had identified more than 2,300 allegations at 308 religious-run schools, and a redress scheme is expected to follow.

title: Former child actor sues Disney alleging company failed to protect her from on-set abuse
summary: A negligence lawsuit filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court alleges a Disney employee sexually abused a minor actor during a 2001 Disney Channel production and that the company failed to protect her or investigate. Disney could not be reached for comment.

title: Judge rules ex-Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries competent to stand trial on sex trafficking charges
summary: A federal judge in Brooklyn found former Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries mentally fit for trial on sex trafficking and interstate prostitution charges, reversing a 2025 finding. Jeffries is accused of exploiting male models while leading the company; jury selection was set for late October 2026.

title: Pentagon report shows estimated military sexual assaults fell for third straight year
summary: The Pentagon's fiscal 2025 report estimated about 20,500 active-duty members experienced sexual assault, down from earlier surveys, while formal reports rose to nearly 8,000. Advocacy groups questioned whether the decline reflects actual conditions.

title: Phillips Academy alumni report abuse by school's former medical director
summary: Two alumni reported they were sexually abused as students by the boarding school's former medical director, who served from 1992 to 2011 and was later convicted on federal child pornography charges. School leaders invited others to come forward and said they are working with an outside nonprofit on a survivor-centered policy review.

title: Pornhub owner Aylo agrees to pay $120 million to settle child sexual abuse material class actions
summary: Aylo agreed to a $120 million settlement, pending court approval, of two U.S. class actions alleging that videos of minors were uploaded to Pornhub without consent. The company denies the allegations but agreed to identity verification, moderation measures and outside audits.

title: Texas and Roblox clash over discovery in state child-safety lawsuit
summary: Texas's attorney general, who accuses Roblox of marketing itself as safe while failing to protect children from predators, says the company has been slow to turn over documents. Roblox calls the requests overbroad; a tentative trial date is set for 2028.

title: Raleigh rider files $50 million lawsuit against Lyft over alleged assault by driver
summary: A North Carolina rider sued Lyft in Durham County alleging a driver sexually assaulted her during a ride in March 2026; the driver has been criminally charged and indicted. Lyft said it does not comment on pending litigation.

title: Louisiana family sues Roblox and Discord alleging platforms enabled sexual exploitation of a teen
summary: A lawsuit filed in Northern California alleges an adult groomed a Louisiana minor on Roblox and moved the contact to Discord, where exploitation followed. The suit claims both companies misled parents about child safety on their platforms.

title: Ex-Kentucky swim coach settles abuse suit; claims against University of Kentucky head to 2027 trial
summary: A former University of Kentucky head swim coach, previously banned for life by the U.S. Center for SafeSport, settled claims brought by two former swimmers alleging sexual assault and a hostile environment. The lawsuit's claims against the university and its former athletic director remain active, with trial set for May 2027; both deny wrongdoing.

title: Interlochen-commissioned report details decades of abuse allegations against nearly 50 adults
summary: An outside investigation commissioned by the Michigan arts boarding school documented about 70 allegations of sexual abuse by nearly 50 affiliated adults from the 1950s to the 2010s, including Jeffrey Epstein, and cited gaps in oversight and a permissive environment. The school apologized, referred names to law enforcement and created a counseling fund, though some alumni say the response falls short.

title: New Mexico judge orders Meta to pay $567 million and tighten protections for minors
summary: A Santa Fe judge found Meta created a public nuisance and ordered $567 million for a teen mental health fund plus a five-year decree including tighter limits on adult contact with minors and enhanced review of child sexual abuse reports. Meta said it will appeal.

title: Jury orders Harrisville Central School District to pay $3.5M over 1980s teacher abuse
summary: A state Supreme Court jury ordered the Lewis County district to pay $3.5 million to a former student who alleged a teacher abused him in the early 1980s and that the district took no action after his parents reported it to the principal. The teacher died in 2018, and it is unclear whether the district will appeal.

title: B.C. court approves $30M class-action settlement over abuse at two Vancouver Catholic schools
institution: Vancouver College and St. Thomas More Collegiate
summary: The B.C. Supreme Court approved a $30-million settlement of a class action by more than 200 former students alleging historical sexual, physical and psychological abuse at the two schools, including by Christian Brothers transferred from Newfoundland's Mount Cashel orphanage. The deal sets up a confidential claims process instead of a trial.

title: Court approves $3M attorney fee deal in FCI Dublin sexual abuse class action
summary: A federal court approved a $3 million settlement covering attorneys' fees in the class action over staff sexual abuse of women at the now-closed FCI Dublin. Related litigation has produced roughly $130 million in payouts to more than 130 former prisoners.

title: Nine more former detainees allege sexual abuse at Clark County juvenile detention center
summary: Nine adults filed notices of intent to sue Clark County, alleging county employees sexually abused them as youths held at the juvenile center between 1990 and 2014. The claims bring the total number of claimants against the county to 17.

title: Snohomish and Pierce counties ask court to make Washington state liable for juvenile abuse claims
summary: Prosecutors for two Washington counties asked a judge to designate the state as the proper defendant in sexual abuse claims tied to county juvenile detention centers, arguing state-appointed judges controlled staffing. The counties estimate potential exposure in the hundreds of millions of dollars.

title: Weill Cornell Medicine reaches compliance deal ending federal probe tied to convicted urologist
summary: Weill Cornell agreed to fund a $30 million patient-safety institute and strengthen abuse prevention to resolve a federal criminal investigation over its handling of former urologist Darius Paduch, who was sentenced to life for abusing patients. The institution previously agreed to pay more than $1 billion to settle civil claims.

title: Former WWE employee's suit against Vince McMahon and WWE moves to private arbitration
summary: A former WWE employee who accused ex-chairman Vince McMahon of sex trafficking and abuse agreed with McMahon and WWE to resolve her federal lawsuit in private arbitration, with the court case to be dismissed. McMahon has denied the allegations.

title: Eight more former detainees sue San Diego County over alleged abuse in juvenile facilities
institution: San Diego County Probation / juvenile detention facilities
summary: Eight anonymous plaintiffs filed a federal lawsuit alleging guards sexually abused them while they were held in San Diego County juvenile facilities. The case adds to similar claims from hundreds of former residents.

title: Southwest Airlines sued over alleged in-flight sexual assault by intoxicated passenger
summary: A passenger alleges Southwest allowed an intoxicated man to board a Seattle-to-Sacramento flight and served him more alcohol before he assaulted her; the man pleaded guilty in federal court to simple assault. The negligence suit claims the airline failed to train staff and follow its own policies.

title: Education Secretary issues teacher sexual misconduct guidance, opens probes into 20 districts
institution: U.S. K-12 districts (including Tulare City and Wilsona, CA; LAUSD)
summary: Following reporting that California failed to revoke credentials of dozens of educators found to have committed sexual misconduct, the U.S. Education Department issued guidance threatening funding for schools that fail to protect students and opened investigations into 20 districts' handling of staff misconduct. It also opened an inquiry into LAUSD's reassignment policy for accused employees.

title: Former detainees file new suit alleging sexual abuse at Snohomish County's Denney juvenile center
institution: Snohomish County, Denney Juvenile Justice Center
summary: Nine former detainees filed a negligence lawsuit alleging staff sexually abused them at the Denney juvenile facilities between the 1980s and 2012. The county said it is reviewing the complaint.

title: Lawsuit accuses Gillespie County of failing to supervise deputy accused of on-duty sexual assault
summary: A woman filed a civil suit alleging a former sheriff's deputy sexually assaulted and harassed her while on duty in 2025, and that the county failed to properly screen and supervise him. The former deputy faces separate pending criminal charges unrelated to sexual assault; the civil claims are allegations.

title: Cook County jury awards $50 million against Peoria climbing camp over assault of young camper
institution: First Ascent Climbing and Fitness Camp
summary: A Cook County jury found the operators of a Peoria children's climbing camp negligent in supervision after a camper was sexually assaulted by another camper in 2022. The award totaled $50 million, including punitive damages.

title: San Francisco Archdiocese reaches $395 million deal with abuse survivors in bankruptcy
source: The New York Times (via GV Wire)
institution: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Francisco
summary: The Archdiocese of San Francisco agreed to pay $395 million to resolve about 530 childhood clergy abuse claims as part of its Chapter 11 case. The deal requires claimant and bankruptcy court approval and includes non-monetary child-protection commitments.

title: Michigan AG report reviews abuse allegations against 38 clergy in Diocese of Saginaw
summary: Michigan's attorney general released a report of more than 250 pages on sexual misconduct allegations involving 37 priests and a deacon in the Diocese of Saginaw, the sixth in a series of statewide reports. No criminal charges resulted, as most incidents predated 2002.

title: New Hampshire YDC abuse fund gets $20 million as new administrator aims to clear 1,700 claims
institution: State of New Hampshire, Youth Development Center settlement fund
summary: Lawmakers allocated $20 million, well below the requested $55 million, to pay claims from people abused at the state's former youth detention center. The fund's new administrator plans to resolve about 1,700 pending claims within three years.

title: UK national grooming gangs inquiry names first areas for investigation
institution: UK National Inquiry into Grooming Gangs
summary: The national statutory inquiry into child sexual exploitation by grooming gangs named London, Bradford, Keighley and Oldham as its first local investigation areas. It will examine how police, councils, health and social services responded.

title: Rhode Island opens two-year window for revived child sexual abuse lawsuits
summary: Governor Dan McKee signed legislation changing the statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims and creating a window through June 2028 for previously time-barred suits against institutions. The law followed a state attorney general report on the Diocese of Providence.

title: Records show South Jersey district paid $3.1M to settle teacher abuse suits
summary: Previously undisclosed settlements released after a public records case show the district and its insurers paid at least $3.125 million over lawsuits alleging a former teacher, who later pleaded guilty, abused boys over more than a decade. Deposition testimony indicated officials had raised boundary concerns years before his arrest, and two suits remain pending.

title: Ohio State trustees approve about $100M settlement with former athletes over team doctor abuse
summary: Ohio State's board approved a preliminary settlement of roughly $100 million covering nearly all of the 280 remaining claimants who said a late university doctor abused them, adding to more than $61 million paid earlier. An independent report previously found university staff knew of complaints as early as 1979 but failed to act.

title: Judge denies Cosby a new trial, upholding $59 million verdict
summary: A Los Angeles County judge rejected Cosby's bid for a new trial, leaving the roughly $59 million civil judgment in place.

title: Complaint filed over alleged sexual abuse of children in Western Australia youth detention
summary: Lawyers lodged a complaint with the Australian Human Rights Commission on behalf of about 100 people alleging sexual abuse in WA's youth detention system, including by custodial staff. A class action may follow if conciliation fails.

title: Harrods redress scheme has fully compensated more than 75 Al Fayed abuse survivors
summary: Harrods' compensation scheme for people abused by former owner Mohamed Al Fayed reports 259 survivors in the process, with more than 75 fully compensated and nearly 200 claims pending. Police and the IOPC continue separate inquiries into enablers and past police handling.

title: Calgary judge approves payouts in John Ware School abuse class action against CBE
institution: Calgary Board of Education (John Ware School)
summary: A judge approved tiered payouts totaling about $15.8 million from the Calgary Board of Education to more than 50 former students who alleged abuse at John Ware School between 1988 and 2004. The board apologized, and the settlement gives survivors a role in shaping policy and training.

title: Uber found liable in second federal bellwether trial over driver misconduct
summary: A federal jury in a North Carolina case found Uber liable for a driver's battery of a rider and awarded $5,000, after the judge ruled Uber is a common carrier under state law. Uber noted jurors found battery rather than sexual assault.

title: Lawsuit against Massage Envy follows sexual abuse charge against Lexington therapist
summary: A client sued Massage Envy in Fayette Circuit Court alleging it failed to supervise staff and implement safeguards after a therapist at its Lexington location was charged with first-degree sexual abuse. The suit also alleges the franchise concealed known risks across its locations.

title: Bankruptcy judge sets claims deadline in El Paso Diocese abuse case
summary: A federal bankruptcy judge set a September deadline for survivors to file abuse claims against the Diocese of El Paso after its Chapter 11 filing. The claims will shape a payment plan that survivors must vote on.

title: Former IU basketball players appeal dismissal of suit over team doctor exams
summary: Five former Indiana University men's basketball players are appealing a federal judge's ruling that their lawsuit, alleging the university and a former head trainer failed to stop abusive exams by a late team doctor, was filed too late. The plaintiffs argue the limitations period should run from when they recognized the conduct as abuse.

title: Cosby seeks new trial, calls $40 million punitive award excessive
summary: Cosby's lawyers moved for a new trial in the 1972 assault case, arguing the punitive damages were excessive and that the judge wrongly excluded certain evidence.

title: Maryland faces potential $60 billion liability from child sex abuse claims against state
summary: More than 12,000 claims have been filed against Maryland government entities under the Child Victims Act, with some lawmakers estimating exposure could reach $60 billion. Questions remain over which damages cap applies and how the state would pay.

title: 11th Circuit revives three sex trafficking lawsuits against metro Atlanta hotels
summary: A federal appeals court reinstated three previously dismissed lawsuits alleging Atlanta-area hotels facilitated trafficking of minors, sending them toward trial. The precedential ruling applies across Georgia, Florida and Alabama.

title: BBC ends contract with Radio 2 host Scott Mills amid reports of closed historical police probe
summary: The BBC said presenter Scott Mills is no longer contracted to it, following media reports linking him to a past police investigation into historical sexual offence allegations. Prosecutors found insufficient evidence to bring charges and the case was closed in 2019; Mills did not comment.

title: Woman sues Planet Fitness alleging assault by known problem patron at South Carolina gym
summary: A member alleges in a negligence suit that another patron sexually assaulted her in a West Ashley Planet Fitness and that staff later described him as a known problem. The company had not responded to requests for comment.

title: New lawsuit accuses Paramus Catholic and Archdiocese of Newark of ignoring coach's abuse
summary: A former student filed a civil suit alleging a former hockey coach abused him on campus and on school trips, and that the school, the Archdiocese of Newark and the Christian Brothers knew and failed to act. It is one of dozens of suits involving the late coach; the archdiocese declined to comment.

title: Santa Fe jury orders Meta to pay New Mexico $375 million in child exploitation case
summary: A jury found Meta willfully violated New Mexico's consumer protection law by misrepresenting platform safety, including the extent of child sexual exploitation, and awarded the state $375 million. Meta said it would appeal.

title: Jury finds Cosby sexually assaulted woman in 1972, awards nearly $60 million
summary: A Santa Monica civil jury found Cosby liable for drugging and assaulting a former restaurant worker in 1972, awarding $19.25 million in compensatory damages and $40 million in punitive damages.

title: California AG finds systemic failures at El Monte Union High School District, imposes court-supervised reforms
institution: El Monte Union High School District
summary: An 18-month state investigation prompted by reporting on misconduct at Rosemead High found systemic shortfalls in how the district responded to sexual abuse and harassment complaints, including discarded disciplinary records. A settlement requires a compliance coordinator, centralized records and four years of court oversight.

title: Federal guard at Brooklyn's MDC indicted on sexual abuse charge
summary: Correctional officer James Johnson was charged in a federal indictment with sexually abusing a detainee in 2025 and lying to federal agents. He was released on bail and has not been convicted.

title: Former students file federal suit alleging Oconto Falls schools ignored staff abuse for years
summary: Three former students sued the Oconto Falls Board of Education in federal court, alleging at least nine staff members groomed or abused at least 14 students between 2005 and 2025 and that the district enabled it. The district says prior allegations were investigated and referred to police; the claims are unproven.

title: Former student files $13.4M claim against Mercer Island School District over alleged teacher abuse
summary: A former student's tort claim alleges administrators received reports about an English teacher's relationship with her in 2012 but conducted a cursory review and did not contact police until 2024. The district declined to comment, citing pending legal proceedings.

title: McDonald's franchisee to pay $80,000 to resolve EEOC harassment suit involving teen worker
summary: An Oklahoma McDonald's franchisee agreed to a consent decree paying $80,000 and adopting anti-harassment policies and training to settle an EEOC suit over harassment of a minor employee. The franchisee denies the allegations.

title: Rhode Island AG report details decades of clergy abuse in Diocese of Providence
summary: Attorney General Peter Neronha released a multi-year investigation into clergy abuse and the diocese's handling of it, summarizing 72 clergy deemed credibly accused. The report recommended reforms including extending certain limitations periods.

title: New Hanover County school board approves settlement tied to convicted former teacher
summary: The board unanimously approved a settlement, reported at $640,000, with three more former students of a science teacher who pleaded guilty in 2019 to dozens of child exploitation charges. Plaintiffs alleged a principal's failure to act allowed the abuse to continue; an earlier case settled for $5.75 million without admission of wrongdoing.

title: LAUSD approves up to $250M more in bonds to pay sexual abuse settlements
summary: The LAUSD board authorized up to $250 million in bonds for abuse settlements, its second such authorization in a year, bringing the total to about $750 million. The wave of claims follows a 2019 state law extending the deadline for childhood abuse claims against public entities.

title: Jewell School District pays $2.35M over claims it ignored complaints about convicted shop teacher
summary: The rural Oregon district settled a federal lawsuit alleging administrators failed to act on multiple complaints about a shop teacher, later convicted of sex crimes, and let him resign quietly and work with younger children elsewhere. The settlement was reached in 2025 but only recently made public.

title: Families pursue legal action against Bright Horizons after nursery worker jailed for child abuse
summary: Former Bright Horizons nursery worker Vincent Chan was sentenced to 18 years after admitting dozens of offences including abuse at a now-closed north London nursery. About 50 families have joined legal action accusing the company of ignoring safeguarding concerns; the company says it is reviewing its practices.

title: Uber loses first federal passenger sexual assault trial with $8.5 million verdict
summary: A federal jury in Phoenix found Uber liable on an apparent-agency theory for a driver's alleged assault of a rider and awarded $8.5 million, while rejecting negligence and design-defect claims. Uber said it would appeal.

title: City of Sanger pays $5.25 million over former officer's sexual assaults
summary: Sanger settled a claim for $5.25 million brought by a woman assaulted by former officer J. DeShawn Torrence, who was convicted in federal court and is serving multiple life sentences. More claims against the city may follow.

title: Winnsboro ISD superintendents arrested on charges of failing to report child abuse
summary: The district's former and current superintendents and another employee were arrested on charges including failure to report child abuse with intent to conceal, with affidavits alleging officials covered up two cases involving staff and students. Their counsel indicated they will plead not guilty.

title: Judge returns LA County foster-care abuse cases to trial track amid settlement delays
institution: Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services
summary: A judge ordered dozens of foster-care abuse lawsuits against Los Angeles County to move toward trial while the county's large juvenile abuse settlement remains in distribution. The court warned that settlement delays do not pause filing deadlines.

title: Women held at LA County jail allege sexual abuse by deputies in federal suit
institution: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, Century Regional Detention Facility
summary: Thirty-eight plaintiffs in a federal case allege widespread sexual misconduct by deputies at the women's jail in Lynwood. The Sheriff's Department says it is investigating the claims.

title: Supreme Court declines to hear challenge to $2.46 billion Boy Scouts abuse settlement
summary: The Supreme Court denied review without comment, leaving the Third Circuit ruling and the plan's third-party releases in place. The decision frees about $1.65 billion in escrowed insurer funds, and Scouting America said payments to survivors could now accelerate.

title: Springfield to pay nearly $15M to settle suits alleging school ignored abuse reports
summary: The city of Springfield agreed to pay close to $15 million to settle two lawsuits alleging a former middle school teacher harassed and assaulted students whose reports to staff were repeatedly dismissed. The school department plans $1 million in staff training on recognizing and reporting grooming.

title: Contract officer pleads guilty to sexually abusing detainee at Louisiana ICE facility
institution: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, South Louisiana ICE Processing Center
summary: Former contract detention officer David Courvelle pleaded guilty in federal court to sexual misconduct with a person in federal custody at the Basile, Louisiana, facility. The charge carries up to 15 years in prison.

title: Federal judge lets WWE 'ring boys' abuse lawsuit proceed to discovery
summary: A federal judge in Maryland allowed a lawsuit to move into discovery that alleges WWE and Vince and Linda McMahon knew of and failed to stop sexual abuse of underage ring crew workers decades ago. Linda McMahon's lawyer called the suit baseless.

title: Women sue Match Group alleging Hinge and Tinder let convicted Denver doctor keep using apps
summary: Six women allege in Denver District Court that Match Group's apps kept recommending Stephen Matthews, later convicted of multiple sexual assaults, after receiving complaints about him. Match Group said it is committed to improving its safety tools.

title: Florida attorney general sues Roblox over alleged failure to protect children from predators
summary: Florida's attorney general sued Roblox alleging it facilitates sexual exploitation of minors and misrepresents its safety, in violation of state consumer protection law. Roblox said the suit misrepresents how its platform works.

title: Federal judge approves Archdiocese of New Orleans bankruptcy plan with abuse fund
institution: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New Orleans
summary: A federal judge confirmed a plan ending the archdiocese's long bankruptcy, including a $230 million compensation fund for clergy abuse survivors. Additional money is expected from an insurer and parishes.

title: Scouting America urges Supreme Court to reject challenge to its bankruptcy deal
summary: The organization told the justices the petitioners represent a tiny fraction of claimants and that the $1.65 billion insurance-rights sale funding the trust closed years ago and cannot be undone. It argued bankruptcy law bars the relief sought.

title: Chicago Board of Education approves $17.5M settlement over former dean's abuse of student
institution: Chicago Public Schools (Greater Lawndale High School for Social Justice)
summary: The board approved a $17.5 million settlement with a former student abused by a dean of students who was convicted and sentenced to 22 years; the suit alleged staff saw warning signs and did not act. CPS denied wrongdoing but said it settled to avoid the toll of a trial.

title: Danny Masterson asks court to overturn rape convictions over attorney errors
summary: Danny Masterson filed a habeas petition arguing his trial lawyers were ineffective and asking that his convictions and sentence be vacated.

title: California judge denies Roblox bid to force child exploitation lawsuit into arbitration
summary: A San Mateo County judge rejected Roblox's motion to compel arbitration in a family's suit alleging its child was exploited after contact on Roblox and Discord, keeping the case in open court. Roblox said it would appeal.

title: Former foster parents sue Clearfield County child welfare agency over undisclosed abuse history
institution: Clearfield County Children, Youth and Family Services
summary: A former foster couple filed a federal lawsuit alleging the county agency placed a teen in their home without disclosing his history of abusing other children, leading to harm in the household. The claims are allegations.

title: Guam-based abuse claimants ask Supreme Court to review Boy Scouts settlement
summary: A group of Guam-based claimants petitioned the Supreme Court, arguing the plan's releases for local councils, churches and schools conflict with the Purdue Pharma ruling. The petition kept roughly $1.5 billion in escrow, leaving survivors with about 1.5% recoveries so far.

title: Varsity Brands and former owner Bain Capital named in $200 million cheer abuse lawsuit
summary: A Gwinnett County, Georgia, lawsuit alleges Varsity Brands, Bain Capital, USA Cheer and others failed to safeguard young athletes from a cheer coach accused of sexual exploitation, including RICO claims. Varsity rejects the claim that it enabled such conduct.

title: Appeals delays leave Boy Scouts abuse survivors waiting on bulk of settlement payouts
summary: Bloomberg Law reported that continuing appeals were holding up full distributions from the survivor trust. Most insurer money remained in escrow pending final resolution of the challenges.

title: Ed Henry accuser settles sex-trafficking suit on eve of trial
summary: The former producer settled her claims against Henry one day before trial; her lawyers said they would appeal the dismissal of Fox News to the Second Circuit.

title: Third Circuit declines to rehear challenge to Boy Scouts Chapter 11 plan
summary: The appeals court refused panel and en banc rehearing of its May ruling upholding the plan. Objecting claimants could next petition the Supreme Court.

title: Third Circuit upholds Boy Scouts bankruptcy plan, saying it is too late to unwind
summary: The Third Circuit rejected appeals by a small group of claimants and holdout insurers, ruling the plan had been consummated too far to be reversed despite the Supreme Court's 2024 Purdue Pharma decision on third-party releases. The trust can keep paying about 82,000 claimants.

title: Defrocked former cardinal Theodore McCarrick dies at 94 without facing trial
summary: McCarrick, the highest-ranking U.S. churchman to be dismissed from the priesthood over sexual abuse, died in Missouri at age 94. Both criminal cases against him had ended with findings that he was not competent to stand trial.

title: Judge dismisses Fox News from sexual assault lawsuit against Ed Henry
summary: A federal judge ruled Fox lacked notice of Henry's alleged conduct before 2020 and dismissed the network from the suit, leaving claims against Henry for trial.

title: Carol Folt, hired after Tyndall scandal, to retire as USC president
summary: Folt announced her retirement, with her tenure credited with addressing the Tyndall-era scandals but criticized over other campus issues.

title: Justice Department agrees to $138.7 million settlement over FBI's Nassar failures
summary: The Justice Department agreed to pay $138.7 million to resolve claims from 139 people who said the FBI's failure to act on 2015 reports allowed Nassar's abuse to continue.

title: Les Moonves to pay Los Angeles ethics fine over interference in police probe
summary: Les Moonves agreed to pay $11,250 to resolve a Los Angeles Ethics Commission complaint that he induced a retired LAPD captain to share confidential details of a 2017 sexual assault report against him.

title: Criminal case against Tyndall formally dismissed after his death
summary: A judge dismissed the criminal case against Tyndall following his death, ending the prosecution without a verdict.

title: Wisconsin judge suspends criminal case against McCarrick, finding him unfit for trial
summary: A Walworth County judge suspended McCarrick's sexual assault case after ruling he was mentally incompetent to stand trial and unlikely to regain competency, mirroring the earlier Massachusetts outcome.

title: Medical examiner attributes Tyndall's death to natural causes
summary: The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner reported that Tyndall died of cardiovascular disease.

title: New competency exam leaves McCarrick's Wisconsin sexual assault case in doubt
summary: A state psychologist's evaluation of McCarrick, charged in Walworth County, Wisconsin, with a 1977 sexual assault at a lake resort, raised doubts about whether the case could proceed to trial.

title: George Tyndall found dead at home while awaiting trial
summary: Tyndall, 76, was found dead at his Los Angeles home before his criminal trial, leaving the charges unresolved.

title: Danny Masterson sentenced to 30 years to life in prison
summary: A Los Angeles judge sentenced Danny Masterson to 30 years to life for two rape convictions after victims gave impact statements in court.

title: Massachusetts judge dismisses McCarrick sex abuse case after finding him not competent for trial
summary: A Dedham judge dismissed the criminal case against McCarrick, 93, after a prosecution expert agreed with the defense that dementia left him unable to assist in his own defense.

title: Tyndall pleads not guilty to 27 felony counts ahead of trial
summary: Tyndall entered not-guilty pleas to 18 counts of sexual penetration and nine counts of sexual battery remaining in the case.

title: Tyndall ordered to stand trial on sexual assault charges
summary: After a preliminary hearing, a judge ruled there was sufficient evidence for Tyndall to stand trial on charges involving 16 patients.

title: Kevin Spacey acquitted on all sexual offense charges in London
summary: A Southwark Crown Court jury found Kevin Spacey not guilty of nine sexual offense charges brought by four men dating to 2001-2013.

title: Nassar stabbed by another inmate in federal prison
summary: Nassar was stabbed multiple times by another inmate at a federal prison in Florida and was hospitalized in stable condition.

title: Fox pays $12 million to settle ex-producer's suit alleging sexism on Tucker Carlson show
summary: Fox settled for $12 million a former producer's suits alleging a misogynistic, hostile workplace on Tucker Carlson's show and coercion in the Dominion case.

title: Nine more women sue Cosby in Nevada under new law lifting time limits
summary: Nine women filed a federal lawsuit in Las Vegas alleging Cosby drugged and assaulted them decades ago, after Nevada eliminated the statute of limitations for such civil claims. Cosby's spokesman denied the allegations.

title: Danny Masterson convicted of two counts of rape at retrial
summary: A Los Angeles jury convicted Danny Masterson of raping two women and deadlocked on a third count. He was taken into custody.

title: Illinois attorney general finds 451 Catholic clergy abused nearly 2,000 children
summary: A nearly five-year investigation by Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul identified 451 Catholic clergy and lay employees who abused 1,997 children in the state's six dioceses since 1950, far more than the church had publicly acknowledged.

title: Jury selection begins in Danny Masterson rape retrial
summary: Danny Masterson's retrial on three rape counts began in Los Angeles, with the judge again permitting limited testimony about the Church of Scientology.

title: Maryland attorney general report details abuse of more than 600 children in Archdiocese of Baltimore
summary: A redacted report from the Maryland attorney general accused more than 150 clergy and others affiliated with the Archdiocese of Baltimore of abusing over 600 children across eight decades and documented a long-running cover-up by church officials.

title: Five women sue Cosby and NBCUniversal under New York Adult Survivors Act
summary: Five women, including former Cosby Show actresses Lili Bernard and Eden Tirl, sued Cosby for assault and named NBCUniversal and two production companies as defendants on negligence claims under New York's one-year lookback window. Cosby's spokesman called the suit frivolous.

title: Danny Masterson rape trial ends in mistrial after jury deadlocks
summary: A Los Angeles judge declared a mistrial after jurors could not reach unanimous verdicts on any of the three rape counts against Danny Masterson; prosecutors said they would retry him.

title: CBS and Moonves to pay $30.5 million to resolve New York attorney general probe
summary: The New York attorney general said CBS executives worked to conceal assault allegations against Les Moonves, including tips from an LAPD captain, while Moonves sold stock; CBS, Paramount and Moonves agreed to pay $30.5 million, most of it to shareholders, and adopt reforms.

title: Jury finds Kevin Spacey not liable in Anthony Rapp lawsuit
summary: A federal civil jury in Manhattan found Anthony Rapp had not proven that Kevin Spacey touched him sexually in 1986, rejecting his $40 million claim.

title: New book by LA Times reporter details how USC scandals nearly went untold
summary: Times journalist Paul Pringle published an account of the reporting behind the Tyndall and Puliafito stories and the obstacles the newsroom faced.

title: Judge confirms $2.46 billion Boy Scouts reorganization plan for more than 80,000 abuse claimants
summary: Bankruptcy Judge Laurie Selber Silverstein approved a $2.46 billion plan funded by the BSA, local councils, settling insurers and sponsoring organizations, which in return are shielded from Scout-related abuse suits. A $250 million deal with the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints was dropped after the judge found its release too broad, and objectors said they would appeal.

title: Civil jury finds Cosby sexually abused a teenager at Playboy Mansion in 1975
summary: A Santa Monica jury found Cosby liable for sexually abusing a 16-year-old girl in 1975 and awarded her $500,000 in damages. Cosby, who denied the claim, did not attend the trial.

title: Kevin Spacey charged in UK with sexual assault of three men
summary: The Crown Prosecution Service authorized four sexual assault charges against Kevin Spacey involving three men in incidents from 2005 to 2013; further charges were added later. Spacey denied the allegations.

title: Preliminary hearing continues in Tyndall criminal case
summary: Former patients testified as the lengthy preliminary hearing on the felony charges against Tyndall continued.

title: USC settles suits with 80 former students over campus doctor Dennis Kelly
summary: USC settled lawsuits brought by 80 former students, mostly gay and bisexual men, who alleged sexual misconduct by former men's health physician Dennis Kelly; terms were not disclosed.

title: Nassar survivors file claims against the FBI
summary: Dozens of survivors filed administrative claims against the FBI over its mishandling of 2015 reports about Nassar, the first step toward suing the federal government.

title: Paramount and Moonves agree to $14.75 million settlement with CBS shareholders
summary: Paramount Global and Les Moonves agreed to pay $14.75 million to settle a securities class action alleging CBS misled investors about its handling of misconduct allegations against Moonves.

title: U.S. Supreme Court declines to review ruling that freed Cosby
summary: The Supreme Court turned down Montgomery County prosecutors' request to reinstate Cosby's conviction, ending the criminal case.

title: Ending forced arbitration for harassment claims signed into law, backed by Gretchen Carlson
summary: President Biden signed a law barring mandatory arbitration of sexual assault and harassment claims; Carlson, whose Fox contract had an arbitration clause, championed the bill.

title: Appeals court revives Masterson accusers' harassment suit against Scientology
summary: A California appeals court reversed an order sending the women's harassment claims to Scientology religious arbitration, allowing their lawsuit against the church and Masterson to proceed in court.

title: Appeals court upholds dismissal of charges against Simon
summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of charges against Simon and criticized the prosecution's investigation.

title: Nassar survivors reach $380 million settlement with USA Gymnastics and USOPC
summary: A bankruptcy judge approved a $380 million settlement among USA Gymnastics, the USOPC, their insurers and hundreds of survivors, ending the bankruptcy case.

title: Kevin Spacey ordered to pay $31 million to 'House of Cards' producer over firing losses
summary: Court filings showed an arbitrator ordered Kevin Spacey to pay about $31 million to MRC, finding he breached his contract's harassment policies and caused losses when the studio rewrote House of Cards.

title: USC admits troubling delay in warning campus about fraternity drugging and assault reports
summary: President Carol Folt acknowledged USC was slow to alert students to reports of drugging and sexual assault allegedly connected to a campus fraternity.

title: Former Cosby Show actress Lili Bernard sues Cosby in New Jersey
summary: Actress Lili Bernard, who appeared on The Cosby Show, filed a civil suit alleging Cosby drugged and sexually assaulted her in 1990, using a New Jersey law that extended filing deadlines. Cosby denied the allegations.

title: Tyndall accusers call for investigation of top USC officials
summary: Former patients and their advocates urged authorities to investigate whether USC administrators knew of Tyndall's alleged abuse and failed to act.

title: Biles, Maroney, Raisman and Nichols testify to Senate about FBI failures
summary: Four elite gymnasts told the Senate Judiciary Committee the FBI ignored and mishandled their reports, following a Justice Department inspector general report criticizing agents; FBI Director Christopher Wray apologized.

title: Judge lets sex-trafficking and assault claims against Ed Henry proceed
source: New York Daily News (via Wigdor LLP)
summary: A federal judge in Manhattan declined to dismiss key claims in the lawsuit against Henry, including sex-trafficking allegations, and allowed some claims against Fox to continue.

title: Fox Business producer sues alleging unwanted advances by Andrew Napolitano
summary: An associate producer sued Fox News alleging unwanted advances by legal analyst Andrew Napolitano and a dismissive response from management. Fox said it took action on the Napolitano complaint and called other claims baseless.

title: Ex-cardinal McCarrick criminally charged in Massachusetts with assaulting a teenager in 1974
summary: McCarrick was charged in Dedham District Court with indecent assault and battery on a person over 14, stemming from an alleged 1974 assault at a wedding reception at Wellesley College. He became the first U.S. cardinal criminally charged with sexual abuse of a minor.

title: Pennsylvania Supreme Court overturns Cosby conviction; he is freed from prison
summary: The state Supreme Court vacated Cosby's conviction, ruling that a former district attorney's earlier promise not to prosecute should have barred the charges, and released him after nearly three years in prison. The ruling did not find him innocent.

title: New York City fines Fox News $1 million over harassment and retaliation
summary: The NYC Commission on Human Rights fined Fox News $1 million, its largest such penalty, and required policy changes after finding harassment and retaliation violations.

title: Parole board denies Cosby release after he refuses sex offender treatment
summary: The Pennsylvania parole board denied Cosby parole, citing his refusal to take part in a required sex offender treatment program.

title: Tyndall settlement leaves some survivors bitter over payout disparities
summary: The Times reported wide disparities between payments to plaintiffs in the state-court deal and those in the federal class settlement.

title: USC agrees to $852 million settlement, bringing Tyndall payouts above $1.1 billion
summary: USC reached an $852 million settlement with about 710 women in state court, which with the federal class deal brought total payouts to more than $1.1 billion, the largest sexual abuse settlement in higher education history.

title: Former Olympic coach John Geddert charged, then dies by suicide
summary: Michigan's attorney general charged Geddert with human trafficking, sexual assault and other crimes; he was found dead hours later.

title: Judge declines to halt Weinstein Company plan pending objectors' appeal
summary: The bankruptcy judge refused a request from objecting accusers to pause the confirmed plan while they appealed.

title: Bankruptcy judge approves Weinstein Company plan with about $17 million for accusers
summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge confirmed a liquidation plan setting aside roughly $17 million for people with sexual misconduct claims against Weinstein.

title: Appeals court rejects Nassar's bid for a new sentencing hearing
summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals ruled that Judge Aquilina's comments did not show bias and denied Nassar's request for resentencing.

title: Empowering Athletes Act strengthens oversight of U.S. Olympic system
summary: A federal law enacted in late 2020 gave Congress power to dissolve the USOPC board and decertify governing bodies, and increased funding for the U.S. Center for SafeSport.

title: Vatican report finds church leaders, including John Paul II, discounted warnings about McCarrick
summary: The Vatican released a 449-page internal report concluding that bishops, cardinals and popes received reports of McCarrick's misconduct for decades, and that Pope John Paul II promoted him despite those warnings.

title: Tyndall pleads not guilty to new felony charges
summary: Tyndall entered not-guilty pleas to the additional charges involving alleged crimes between 2011 and 2015.

title: Lawsuit accuses Ed Henry of rape and names other Fox hosts in harassment claims
summary: A former Fox Business associate producer sued alleging Henry sexually assaulted her, and a former guest commentator joined with harassment claims against several hosts. Henry and Fox denied the allegations.

title: Report: Ousted USC president Nikias received $7.6 million payout
summary: Tax filings showed Nikias received about $7.6 million in compensation after he was pushed out over the Tyndall scandal.

title: Federal judge rejects proposed $18.9 million Weinstein settlement
summary: U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein refused to approve a class settlement negotiated with the New York attorney general's office, criticizing how it treated different claimants.

title: Six more felony counts filed against Tyndall
summary: Prosecutors added six counts of sexual assault and battery involving five additional women, bringing the total to 35 felony counts.

title: Fox News fires anchor Ed Henry after sexual misconduct complaint
summary: Fox fired America's Newsroom co-anchor Ed Henry after an investigation into a former employee's complaint of willful sexual misconduct years earlier.

title: Danny Masterson charged with raping three women
summary: The Los Angeles County district attorney charged Danny Masterson with three counts of rape involving incidents between 2001 and 2003. Masterson pleaded not guilty.

title: Judge dismisses charges against former MSU President Simon
summary: An Eaton County judge dismissed the charges against Simon, finding insufficient evidence that she lied to investigators.

title: Weinstein sentenced to 23 years in prison
summary: Justice James Burke sentenced Weinstein to 23 years in prison for his New York convictions.

title: Education Department finds USC failed students in Tyndall case; reforms required
summary: The Office for Civil Rights concluded USC systemically failed to respond to complaints about Tyndall and entered a resolution agreement requiring Title IX reforms and monitoring.

title: Jury convicts Weinstein of rape and criminal sexual act, acquits on most serious counts
summary: A Manhattan jury found Weinstein guilty of third-degree rape and a first-degree criminal sexual act but acquitted him of predatory sexual assault.

title: Boy Scouts of America files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy amid wave of abuse lawsuits
summary: The Boy Scouts filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware, pausing hundreds of lawsuits brought after states including New York, New Jersey, Arizona and California opened lookback windows for old abuse claims. The organization planned a survivor compensation trust; its internal files listed 7,819 suspected abusers.

title: USA Gymnastics settlement proposal includes Twistars and Geddert contributions
summary: A proposed USA Gymnastics bankruptcy settlement with Nassar survivors included added payments from Twistars and the Gedderts; survivors did not accept the initial plan.

title: Actress Annabella Sciorra testifies against Weinstein at New York trial
summary: Sciorra testified that Weinstein raped her in the early 1990s; her account was offered to support the predatory sexual assault charges.

title: Police search home and gym of coach John Geddert
summary: Investigators searched the home and former gym of Geddert, the 2012 Olympic women's coach who worked closely with Nassar.

title: Cosby asks Pennsylvania Supreme Court to review his conviction
summary: Cosby's lawyers petitioned the state's highest court to overturn his conviction after losing in the Superior Court; the court later agreed to hear the appeal.

title: Federal judge says he will approve USC's $215 million Tyndall class settlement
summary: U.S. District Judge Stephen Wilson said he was inclined to grant final approval to the federal class settlement and to appoint a special master to oversee individual awards.

title: Weinstein's New York rape trial begins as Los Angeles prosecutors file new charges
summary: Jury selection began in Manhattan the same day the Los Angeles County district attorney announced rape and sexual battery charges against Weinstein involving two women.

title: Attorney general's investigation of MSU's Nassar handling suspended
summary: Michigan's attorney general halted the state's inquiry into Michigan State after the university refused to release privileged documents.

title: Weinstein and former studio reach tentative $25 million deal with accusers
summary: A tentative global settlement funded by insurers would resolve many civil claims against Weinstein and The Weinstein Company's former board without Weinstein admitting wrongdoing.

title: Fox Nation host Britt McHenry sues Fox alleging harassment by co-host
summary: Fox Nation host Britt McHenry sued Fox News alleging sexual harassment by co-host George 'Tyrus' Murdoch and retaliation; Fox and Murdoch disputed the claims.

title: Pennsylvania Superior Court upholds Cosby conviction
summary: A state appeals panel rejected Cosby's challenges, including to the testimony of other accusers and the prosecution's handling of a former DA's non-prosecution promise.

title: Los Angeles prosecutors decline Kevin Spacey case after accuser's death
summary: The Los Angeles County district attorney declined to file a sexual battery case against Kevin Spacey because the masseur who accused him had died.

title: Matt Lauer accused of rape by former NBC colleague in Farrow book
summary: A former NBC News employee whose 2017 complaint led to Matt Lauer's firing alleged in Ronan Farrow's book Catch and Kill that Lauer raped her in 2014. Lauer denied the allegation, saying the encounter was consensual.

title: California law reopens filing window for Tyndall survivors
summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 1510, allowing former patients of Tyndall to revive claims that would otherwise be time-barred; USC had lobbied against the bill.

title: Tyndall released from jail after posting bail
summary: Tyndall was released from custody after posting bail while awaiting trial on the felony charges.

title: Masterson accusers sue Danny Masterson and Church of Scientology over alleged stalking
summary: Four women who had accused Danny Masterson of rape filed a civil suit alleging Scientology members stalked and harassed them after they reported him to police. Masterson and the church denied the claims.

title: Cosby's insurer settles Janice Dickinson defamation suit over his denials
summary: Cosby's insurer, AIG, settled a defamation lawsuit brought by model Janice Dickinson over statements his representatives made dismissing her rape allegation; Cosby's camp objected to the settlement.

title: Massachusetts prosecutors drop sexual assault case against Kevin Spacey
summary: The Cape and Islands district attorney dropped the indecent assault charge against Kevin Spacey after the accuser declined to testify amid a dispute over his missing phone.

title: Judge lowers Tyndall's bail to $1.6 million
summary: A judge reduced Tyndall's bail from $2.1 million to $1.6 million after a hearing in which prosecutors cited evidence seized in the investigation.

title: Tyndall pleads not guilty to sexual abuse charges
summary: Tyndall pleaded not guilty to all 29 felony counts at his arraignment in Los Angeles.

title: Detectives seek to identify women in videos and photos seized from Tyndall
summary: Authorities said they recovered thousands of videos and photos during the investigation and were working to identify women depicted.

title: George Tyndall arrested and charged with 29 felonies involving 16 patients
summary: LAPD arrested Tyndall and Los Angeles County prosecutors charged him with sexual penetration and sexual battery counts involving 16 women treated at the student health center.

title: Bryan Singer agrees to $150,000 settlement of sexual assault lawsuit
summary: Bryan Singer agreed to pay $150,000 to resolve a lawsuit alleging he sexually assaulted a 17-year-old at a 2003 party, in a settlement reached through bankruptcy proceedings. Singer continued to deny wrongdoing.

title: Judge grants preliminary approval of USC's $215 million class settlement
summary: U.S. District Judge Stephen Wilson granted preliminary approval to the federal class-action settlement for Tyndall's former patients.

title: Unsealed records show USC was warned Tyndall could be targeting Asian students
summary: Confidential documents released in litigation showed outside medical reviewers had warned USC that Tyndall might be preying on Asian international students.

title: Twistars gymnastics club settles Nassar lawsuits for $2.1 million
summary: The Michigan gym owned by former Olympic coach John Geddert, where Nassar treated athletes, agreed to a $2.1 million settlement with survivors.

title: New suits filed against USC over Tyndall and men's health doctor Dennis Kelly
summary: Additional lawsuits were filed against USC over two former campus doctors, including claims by at least 30 gay and bisexual men against Dennis Kelly.

title: Federal judge delays preliminary approval of $215 million Tyndall settlement
summary: A federal judge held off on preliminary approval of the class settlement, citing questions about how payments would be distributed.

title: Los Angeles Times wins Pulitzer Prize for Tyndall investigation
summary: The Times won the Pulitzer Prize for investigative reporting for its series exposing Tyndall's conduct and USC's response.

title: Questions raised over how much of USC's internal Tyndall investigation will stay secret
summary: The Times reported that the findings of a trustee-commissioned outside investigation into the Tyndall affair might never be made public.

title: USC names Carol Folt president as it tries to move past scandals
summary: USC chose former UNC chancellor Carol Folt as its 12th president following Nikias's ouster over the Tyndall scandal.

title: State judge orders USC to produce internal Tyndall records
summary: A Los Angeles Superior Court judge ordered USC to turn over internal records to attorneys representing hundreds of plaintiffs in the state litigation.

title: Gay and bisexual former students sue USC over campus men's health doctor
summary: Former students filed suit alleging sexual misconduct by former USC men's health physician Dennis Kelly, prompting a campus protest over the health center; Kelly denied wrongdoing.

title: Vatican defrocks former cardinal Theodore McCarrick over sexual abuse
summary: Pope Francis confirmed a Vatican ruling that found McCarrick guilty under church law of sexually abusing minors and adults and dismissed him from the priesthood, the first cardinal laicized for abuse.

title: Revised $215 million settlement agreement filed in federal court
summary: USC filed its formal class-action settlement agreement detailing payment tiers and reforms, even as federal regulators continued investigating.

title: Atlantic investigation details new sexual abuse allegations against Bryan Singer
summary: An investigation by The Atlantic reported allegations from several men who said Bryan Singer sexually abused them when they were teenagers. Singer called the report a homophobic smear and denied the claims.

title: John Engler resigns as Michigan State interim president
summary: Engler resigned under pressure after comments about Nassar survivors drew widespread condemnation.

title: Kevin Spacey charged with indecent assault in Nantucket case
summary: Massachusetts prosecutors charged Kevin Spacey with felony indecent assault and battery over a 2016 encounter with an 18-year-old at a Nantucket bar. Spacey denied the charge.

title: CBS denies Les Moonves $120 million severance after board investigation
summary: The CBS board concluded after an outside investigation that it had grounds to fire Les Moonves for cause, including willful failure to cooperate, and denied him a $120 million severance package.

title: Police found trove of nude images in Tyndall's storage unit, sources say
summary: Investigators reportedly recovered large numbers of images of women from a storage unit tied to Tyndall early in the LAPD probe.

title: USA Gymnastics files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: USA Gymnastics filed for bankruptcy protection in Indianapolis, pausing hundreds of lawsuits from Nassar survivors and the USOC decertification process.

title: Grand jury convened to hear evidence against ex-USC gynecologist
summary: Los Angeles County prosecutors convened a criminal grand jury to hear evidence about Tyndall's alleged abuse of patients.

title: Former MSU President Lou Anna Simon charged with lying to police
summary: Simon was charged with lying to state police investigators about what she knew of a 2014 complaint against Nassar. She denied wrongdoing.

title: U.S. Olympic Committee moves to revoke USA Gymnastics' governing status
summary: The USOC began proceedings to decertify USA Gymnastics as the sport's national governing body over its handling of the Nassar crisis.

title: USC agrees to tentative $215 million class-action settlement with Tyndall patients
summary: USC announced a proposed $215 million federal class-action settlement covering former patients of Tyndall, with tiered payments and campus reforms.

title: More than 250 women file state-court suits against USC, rejecting class deal
summary: Attorneys for more than 250 former Tyndall patients filed lawsuits in state court and criticized the proposed federal settlement.

title: Justice Department opens federal investigation into clergy abuse in Pennsylvania dioceses
summary: Federal prosecutors in Pennsylvania served subpoenas on Catholic dioceses across the state, opening the first known federal investigation into clergy sexual abuse and its concealment in the wake of the grand jury report.

title: Former USA Gymnastics CEO Steve Penny arrested on evidence tampering charge
summary: Penny was arrested on a Texas indictment accusing him of removing documents from the Karolyi Ranch related to the Nassar investigation.

title: Prosecutors drop one count in Weinstein criminal case
summary: A judge dismissed one sexual assault count at prosecutors' request after questions arose about the investigation, while the remaining charges stood.

title: Fox settles remaining claims in Scottie Nell Hughes retaliation suit
summary: Hughes settled her remaining retaliation claims with Fox for an undisclosed amount after a judge earlier dismissed her assault claim and other counts.

title: Cosby sentenced to 3 to 10 years in state prison, labeled sexually violent predator
summary: A Montgomery County judge sentenced Cosby to three to 10 years in state prison and designated him a sexually violent predator; he was taken into custody immediately.

title: New allegations against Les Moonves emerge in second New Yorker report
summary: A follow-up report detailed accounts from six additional women accusing Les Moonves of sexual misconduct, as CBS negotiated his exit.

title: Les Moonves resigns as CBS chairman and CEO
summary: Les Moonves stepped down from CBS hours after new allegations were published; CBS and Moonves pledged $20 million to groups supporting the #MeToo movement, deducted from any severance.

title: Judge denies Nassar's request for a new sentencing hearing
summary: An Eaton County judge rejected Nassar's bid for resentencing and a new judge, which argued his sentences were tainted by bias.

title: USC restructures student health center in wake of Tyndall scandal
summary: USC leaders described staffing and oversight changes at the Engemann Student Health Center aimed at rebuilding student trust.

title: Tyndall's medical license suspended pending state medical board decision
summary: Tyndall was barred from practicing medicine while the Medical Board of California weighed a final decision on his license.

title: Olympians Kyla Ross and Madison Kocian say Nassar abused them
summary: Two members of U.S. Olympic teams said publicly that they were also among Nassar's victims.

title: Pennsylvania grand jury report says more than 300 priests abused over 1,000 children in six dioceses
summary: A statewide grand jury report released by the Pennsylvania attorney general identified more than 300 accused priests and over 1,000 child victims across six dioceses over seven decades. It concluded that church leaders systematically covered up the abuse.

title: Nikias formally steps down; Wanda Austin becomes interim USC president
summary: Nikias left the presidency earlier than planned after calls to hasten his departure, with trustee Wanda Austin named interim president.

title: New Yorker reports misconduct allegations against CBS chief Les Moonves
summary: A Ronan Farrow investigation reported that six women accused CBS chief executive Les Moonves of sexual harassment or intimidation and described a wider culture of misconduct at CBS; the board said it would investigate. Moonves acknowledged past advances but denied misusing his position.

title: 51 more Tyndall patients sue USC as board chairman pledges expedited inquiry
summary: Fifty-one additional women filed suit against USC and Tyndall, and trustees chairman Rick Caruso said the university's internal investigation would be expedited.

title: Tyndall retains high-profile criminal defense attorney
summary: Tyndall hired prominent Los Angeles defense lawyer Leonard Levine as police continued their investigation and civil suits mounted.

title: Former Fox executive Bill Shine named White House communications chief
summary: Shine, who left Fox amid criticism of how he handled harassment complaints under Ailes, was appointed to a senior White House communications post.

title: Weinstein indicted on additional charges involving a third woman
summary: Prosecutors added charges including predatory sexual assault, which carries a potential life sentence, based on an allegation from a third woman.

title: At least 200 former students join lawsuits against USC over Tyndall
summary: The number of former students suing USC grew to at least 200, alleging the university ignored warnings about Tyndall for nearly 30 years.

title: Cardinal Theodore McCarrick removed from public ministry after abuse allegation found credible
summary: The Vatican ordered retired Washington Archbishop Theodore McCarrick out of public ministry after an Archdiocese of New York review board found credible a decades-old allegation that he abused a teenage altar server. McCarrick denied the allegation.

title: LAPD serves search warrants at ex-USC gynecologist's home and storage unit
summary: Police detectives searched Tyndall's Los Angeles home and a storage facility as part of the criminal investigation into allegations from former patients.

title: Federal Education Department opens investigation into USC's handling of Tyndall complaints
summary: The U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights began investigating whether USC violated Title IX in responding to complaints about its campus gynecologist.

title: Former USA Gymnastics chief Steve Penny invokes the Fifth before Senate panel
summary: At a Senate subcommittee hearing on the Nassar case, Penny declined to answer questions, while Lou Anna Simon and other officials testified.

title: Weinstein pleads not guilty to rape and sex abuse charges
summary: Weinstein entered a not guilty plea in Manhattan court, and his lawyer said he would seek to have the case dismissed.

title: Manhattan grand jury indicts Weinstein on rape and sex crime charges
summary: A grand jury returned an indictment against Weinstein on rape and criminal sexual act charges, formalizing the case brought by the Manhattan district attorney.

title: USC President C.L. Max Nikias agrees to step down
summary: USC's board of trustees announced that Nikias would step down as president amid mounting pressure over the university's handling of the Tyndall complaints.

title: More women sue USC as Tyndall defends himself in letter to The Times
summary: Fourteen more women filed lawsuits alleging Tyndall abused them during exams and that USC ignored complaints, while Tyndall denied wrongdoing in a letter to the newspaper.

title: Harvey Weinstein surrenders to New York police and is charged with rape
summary: Weinstein turned himself in at a Manhattan precinct and was charged with rape and a criminal sexual act involving two women; he was released on $1 million bail.

title: About 300 former patients come forward as LAPD begins Tyndall investigation
summary: Roughly 300 people contacted USC about Tyndall and the university began sharing patient information with the Los Angeles Police Department, which opened a criminal investigation.

title: Records show students warned USC about gynecologist early in his career
summary: Former patients said they complained to USC about Tyndall as early as the 1990s, suggesting the university missed early chances to act.

title: USC Academic Senate calls on Nikias to resign
summary: USC's faculty governing body voted to call for President Nikias's resignation following the Tyndall revelations and a series of other campus scandals.

title: 200 USC professors demand President Nikias resign over Tyndall handling
summary: Two hundred USC faculty members signed a letter calling for President C.L. Max Nikias to step down, while the board of trustees initially expressed confidence in him.

title: USC fires two health clinic supervisors amid gynecologist scandal
summary: USC dismissed two supervisors at its student health center over their handling of complaints about Tyndall as reports from former patients poured in.

title: Fox News pays $10 million to settle 18 discrimination and harassment suits
summary: Fox News paid about $10 million to resolve 18 race and gender discrimination claims brought by current and former employees.

title: Michigan State agrees to $500 million settlement with Nassar survivors
summary: MSU agreed to pay $500 million to settle claims from 332 people, the largest settlement of its kind involving a university.

title: LA Times reveals USC let gynecologist keep treating students despite years of complaints
summary: A Los Angeles Times investigation reported that USC received complaints for decades about campus gynecologist George Tyndall's conduct toward young women but allowed him to keep practicing and quietly let him resign in 2017 without reporting him to the medical board.

title: Former USC students describe decades of troubling conduct by campus gynecologist
summary: Former patients spanning several decades told the Times about inappropriate comments and examinations by Tyndall, broadening the account of his time at the student health center.

title: NBC internal review of Lauer finds no evidence news leadership knew of misconduct
summary: An NBC Universal internal investigation concluded that senior news executives were not aware of complaints about Matt Lauer before November 2017 and found no culture of harassment, a finding critics questioned because it was not independent.

title: Bankruptcy judge approves sale of Weinstein Company assets to Lantern Capital
summary: A Delaware bankruptcy judge approved the sale of the studio's film and television assets to Lantern Capital Partners for roughly $289 million.

title: Temple University rescinds Bill Cosby's honorary degree after conviction
summary: Temple's board voted to revoke the honorary degree it awarded Cosby, joining numerous other colleges that withdrew honors after his conviction.

title: Bill Cosby convicted on three counts of aggravated indecent assault at retrial
summary: A jury in Norristown, Pennsylvania, found Cosby guilty of drugging and sexually assaulting Andrea Constand in 2004, making him the first celebrity convicted in the #MeToo era.

title: Prosecutors disclose Cosby paid Constand nearly $3.4 million in 2006 civil settlement
summary: During opening statements at the retrial, prosecutors revealed that Cosby paid about $3.38 million to settle Constand's civil lawsuit in 2006.

title: Weinstein Company files for bankruptcy and releases accusers from nondisclosure agreements
summary: The Weinstein Company filed for Chapter 11 protection in Delaware with a stalking-horse bid from Lantern Capital and said it was ending nondisclosure agreements that had kept accusers silent.

title: Judge allows five additional accusers to testify at Cosby retrial
summary: The trial judge ruled that five other women could testify about alleged prior misconduct at Cosby's retrial, a significant expansion from the single additional accuser allowed in the first trial.

title: Aly Raisman sues U.S. Olympic Committee and USA Gymnastics
summary: Raisman filed suit alleging the USOC and USA Gymnastics knew or should have known about Nassar's abuse and failed to stop it.

title: New York attorney general sues Weinstein Company and Harvey and Bob Weinstein
summary: Attorney General Eric Schneiderman filed a civil rights suit alleging the company failed to protect employees from Harvey Weinstein's harassment, derailing a pending sale of the studio.

title: Michigan State moves to fire former medical dean William Strampel
summary: MSU began proceedings to fire William Strampel, Nassar's former dean at the College of Osteopathic Medicine, over his oversight of Nassar.

title: Nassar sentenced to 40 to 125 years in Eaton County
summary: Judge Janice Cunningham imposed a third prison sentence on Nassar for abuse at the Twistars gym, concluding his criminal cases.

title: Former governor John Engler named interim MSU president
